text.p: One hundred people have been killed and about 4,000 houses destroyed in Nile floods and heavy rains in five of Sudan's 26 states, the official news agency SUNA said on Sunday.
The floods have also done heavy damage to farms and livestock, the agency added, quoting John Dor Majok, chairman of a committee soliciting support for flood victims.
The states affected are Khartoum, White Nile and River Nile in the north and Upper Nile and Jonglei in the south.
The agency did not say what period the death toll covered but the Blue Nile began to rise in early August after exceptionally heavy rain in Ethiopia this season.

The minister's estimate of the number of houses destroyed was much lower than those from other sources. Abdel-Rahman Sir al-Khatim, the governor of River Nile, has said floods destroyed 40,000 houses in his state alone.
Government agencies are planning to send a convoy of relief aid to those affected by the floods in the provinces of Pibor and Sobat in Jonglei and Upper Nile states.

The news agency quoted the rapporteur of Majok's committee as saying it had received a message from Pibor saying floods has washed away 111 villages and killed 30 people in the province, about 1,000 km (600 miles) south of Khartoum.
In Sobat province further north, many people have fled rural areas for the bigger towns and the provincial commissioner has appealed for urgent help, SUNA said.
